sections.heading: Destination Snapshot
sections.body: The Gorges du Verdon are a benchmark limestone multi-pitch destination: huge gorge walls, exposed abseil approaches, technical faces and a level of commitment that gives even moderate grades real weight.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Verdon is not casual roadside sport climbing dressed up as adventure. The gorge is deep, the walls are high, and many routes begin with the psychological shift of descending before you climb.

The reward is exceptional limestone in a dramatic setting. Long technical pitches, slabs, cracks, walls and exposed positions make the place a lifetime venue for roped climbers who want more than quick redpoints.

sections.heading: History
sections.body:
Verdon’s reputation is built on French limestone history and big-wall style commitment. It has influenced generations of climbers because it combines high-quality rock with a serious setting.

That seriousness is part of the destination’s value. Good Verdon days are planned carefully, started early and treated with respect.

sections.heading: Rock and Style
sections.body:
The rock is limestone, often technical and exposed. Expect slabs, cracks, vertical walls and steeper sections rather than one uniform style.

Single-pitch climbing exists in the broader area, but Verdon's strongest identity is long multi-pitch climbing.

sections.heading: Who Is It For
sections.body:
Verdon suits confident roped climbers with multi-pitch systems already in place. It is ideal for teams who like exposure, long days and technical limestone.

It is not a good place to improvise ropework. Less experienced climbers should keep objectives very conservative or climb with someone who knows the style.

sections.heading: Grades and Scale
sections.body:
Verdon has more than 400 multi-pitch routes as a conservative planning scale. There are also single-pitch sectors, but those are best planned separately with a current guidebook.

For planning, choose by route length, descent, aspect and team speed before grade.

sections.heading: Season
sections.body:
Spring and autumn are the core planning windows. Autumn is often the strongest period, spring can be good, summer brings heat and winter can be cold.

Aspect matters in the gorge. A good forecast still needs a route-specific plan.

sections.heading: Gear
sections.body:
Bring a multi-pitch kit, helmets, prusiks or preferred rappel backups, enough quickdraws and anchor material for the chosen route, and a rope system matched to descents.

Check every route against a current topo. In Verdon, approach and descent information are part of the gear list.

sections.heading: Getting There
sections.body:
A car is strongly recommended. The gorge is broad, approaches vary, and daily route choice depends on aspect, parking and descent logistics.

Nimes is a useful airport reference, but exact flight planning should be checked separately before booking.

sections.heading: Stay and Eat
sections.body:
Campsites, hotels and guesthouse-style stays all make sense around the Verdon. Choose a base that keeps drives and early starts realistic.

For a focused climbing trip, easy breakfast, food storage and recovery matter more than being in the busiest village.

sections.heading: Rest Days
sections.body: Rest days can still use the gorge: viewpoints, walking, swimming conditions when safe, and quiet village time. A proper rest day is often the best way to keep later multi-pitch objectives clean.

sections.heading: Tips and Ethics
sections.body:
Plan backwards from the descent and daylight. In Verdon, the crux of the day may be timing, route finding or managing exposure rather than a single move.

Carry current information and do not rely on memory for abseils, fixed gear or restrictions.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body:
Verdon has real commitment. Abseil approaches, exposure, rockfall, heat, storms and slow parties can all change the day quickly.

Wear helmets, know retreat options, start early and keep enough margin to solve problems without rushing.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Verdon mainly multi-pitch? Yes, its strongest identity is long limestone multi-pitch climbing.

When should I go? Spring and autumn are the clearest supported windows.

Is it beginner-friendly? Not as an unguided first multi-pitch venue. Rope skills and conservative planning are essential.
